messages:
maria: quick heads-up: onboarding a HF model (byte-level-ish tokenizer) produced parity issues after conversion. repro input and token dumps below.
kevin: paste the input and both token lists please.
maria: input: \"Resume – Café ﬁrst line: \"Fancy quotes: “Hello”\" and emoji: 🧪\"

maria: HF upstream tokenization (python) ->
```
['Resume', '\u0120\u2013', '\u0120Caf', '\u00e9', '\u0120', '\u0120fi', 'rst', '\u0120line', ':', '\u0120', '\"', 'Fancy', '\u0120quotes', ':', '\u0120\u201c', 'Hello', '\u201d']
```

maria: Converted/Redwood tokenizer produces ->
```
['Resume', ' ', '\u2013', ' ', 'Caf', '\u00e9', ' ', 'fi', 'rst', ' ', 'line', ':', ' ', '\"', 'Fancy', ' ', 'quotes', ':', ' ', '\"Hello\"']
```

maria: two concrete issues: (A) HF uses prefix-space markers (U+0120) and byte-fallback splitting for accents/ligatures, conversion turned these into explicit space tokens; (B) HF normalizer in that tokenizer repo is NFKC and also has ByteLevel pre_tokenizer; our converter dropped normalizer+pre_tokenizer and Redwood chose whitespace pretokenizer by default.
jonah: are we seeing eval differences?
maria: yes. ran a 100-sample smoke eval (chat+code+email). token inflation ~+0.7 tokens/sample median, some role-parsing tests flip because role markers like <assistant> get tokenized differently when spaces inserted. eval-bot flagged 9 failures labeled \"tokenizer-parity\".
eval-bot: flagged tests: ml-onboard/chat-role-parse, doc-gen/header-splits, codefmt/indent-anchor
kevin: what did conversion write into tokenizer config.json?
maria: converter emitted a sanitized fragment like: 
```
{"normalizer": null, "pre_tokenizer": null, "added_tokens": [{"id":32001, "content": "<|system|>"}], "byte_fallback": true}
```
maria: since normalizer/pre_tokenizer were not plain dicts in HF, the mapping dropped them (null) and downstream runtime used defaults. also we treated all added_tokens as single_word=True implicitly which is wrong for some HF entries.
kevin: plan: (1) change converter to copy normalizer & pre_tokenizer verbatim when present; (2) honor added_tokens.single_word flag; (3) add a short-term input-normalize (NFKC) shim for already-converted versions.
maria: quick experiment: applying NFKC to inputs before Redwood tokenization on a staging model shrank token delta to ~+0.02/sample on the smoke set. looks promising as a mitigant.
kevin: i'll add a unit/CI test that runs HF.tokenize vs Redwood.tokenize over a corpus of edge cases: ligatures (ﬁ), em/en-dashes, combining marks, emojis, CJK sequences, and sequences with added_tokens. fail CI if avg token delta > 0.15 or >2 samples mismatch role-boundary.
jonah: please also add a golden-diff reporter in onboarding that prints a small example diff for human review; auto-blaming is harsh.
infra-bot: created INF-2598: \"hf->redwood-tokenizer-parity: preserve normalizer & pre_tokenizer; map single_word for added_tokens\" assigned to @kevin @maria
maria: PR will include: converter change + parity CI test + small script onboarding/scripts/token_parity_report.py which prints HF vs Redwood tokens and highlights added_token collisions.
jonah: once merged I will re-run the full regression suite. if we still see noisy failures, consider a compatibility layer that emulates HF ByteLevel split semantics at tokenization time instead of conversion-time changes.
maria: TL;DR: root cause = conversion stripped HF normalizer and pre-tokenizer behavior and lost added_token single_word semantics -> explicit spaces and token count drift -> cost + parsing regressions. fix = preserve upstream tokenizer fields and add short-term NFKC shim + CI.
kevin: thanks. ping when PR is ready for review.
infra-bot: staged a conversion patch to staging job 5672; post-deploy validation queued.
maria: leaving the quick repro and report script in the ticket for reviewers.
jonah: appreciated, nice repro and clear action items.
